construct.constructDefinition: Assessment: teacher self-positioning on digital-competence maturity statements. Preserves each competence’s A1–C2 statement and separate zero-point not-aware response; not an agreement scale, a teaching-quality measure or an observed performance test. No area/global aggregate is computed by this split unit.

population.populationNotes: Adult primary and secondary teachers able to understand the fixed English Toolkit. Initial digital split scope; age18+ is a project scope, not a source-derived validation cut-off. Source studies do not establish Chinese-language or separate-area digital equivalence. Early-years use on the current website is not borrowed as validation for this fixed primary/secondary version.

administration.timeFrame: Current professional digital practice and experience; no fixed day/week recall period.
layoutConstraints: Choose the ONE original maturity statement that best describes your current competence in each item. Six item-specific A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2 statements are scored1–6, and the seventh not-aware response is scored0.
Keep the original competence order and original option order; no agreement anchors, automatic reversal, simplified alternatives or shortened items.
Six separate native area units are project packaging; independent administration equivalence is not established. The ordinary-composite recipe retains all32 competences in order.
This unit reports each competence separately; no area mean, global192-point total or overall A1–C2 band is manufactured across the split tools.

Missing items remain null; 0 is a real not-aware answer, not missing data. Any unanswered competence makes this area incomplete and suppresses its interpretations; this complete-area policy is a project choice, not an inferred source missing-data algorithm.
Timing is an approximate project allocation of the official circa25-minute whole-tool estimate, not measured timing.

intendedUses.notes: Professional learning self-reflection using a fixed EU source, not a certification, teacher appraisal or observed competence test.
Separate-area digital packaging and local applicability require explicit interpretation limits; not automatic cross-language/role equivalence.

options.label: A1: I am aware that digital technologies can support both formative and summative assessment(e.g. digital quizzes, online polls).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies to support formative and summative assessment(e.g. online quizzes, games, forms, mobile apps).
B1: I use various digital technologies to support formative and summative assessment (e.g. create a digital test, use assessment platforms that offer timely feedback to students).

B2: I select digital technologies to support specific aspects in assessment “of”, “for” and “as” learning and capture best the nature of the learning outcome to be assessed (e.g. self-reflection rubrics, assignments that offer timely feedback to students, shared documents that support peer reviewing/feedback).

C1: I reflect on and involve my students in the design of digitally-supported assessments, selecting digital technologies that best support the assessment purpose and content (e.g. deciding assessment criteria and modality, co-creation of rubrics, design the format of self and peer assessment, formative or summative assessment scaffolding tools).

C2: I propose and promote strategies and digital technologies within my school and its wider community to support assessment “of”, “for” and “as” learning (e.g. self and peer assessment, promotion of transversal skills, work-based assessment, e-portfolios).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that digital technologies can capture students’ learning processes and outcomes (e.g. digital quizzes, online polls, forms, assessment platforms).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies to capture evidence about my students' individual and/or group learning activity (e.g. digital quizzes, online polls, surveys).

B1: I use various digital technologies to collect and analyse evidence of students' individual and/or group learning outcomes and learning processes (e.g. online polls, forms, surveys, learning analytics, spreadsheets).

B2: I select digital technologies that facilitate presentation and analysis of learning data to support my reflections on my teaching practice and on my students' learning (e.g. record and visually represent data, automatically generated graphs, mind mapping tools, digital dashboards).

C1: I reflect on and involve my students in capturing and analysing their learning data, which can be used to plan their future learning (e.g. reflective learning logs, personal goal setting software).

C2: I initiate and promote strategies and practices to help my school and its wider community use digital technologies to evidence learning, and use assessment data to support decision-making for targeted interventions (e.g. pedagogical decisions, administrative decisions such as students' attendance, and data on students' learning such as grades)
I am not aware of this competence.

A1: I am aware that digital technologies can be used to provide feedback to learners including automated feedback (e.g. blogs, online polls, online forms, applications using Artificial Intelligence (AI)).
A2: I have tried using digital technologies that support the integration of feedback and reflection on students' learning (e.g. blogs, wikis, video-based feedback, digital annotation on assignments).

B1: I use various digital technologies to provide timely feedback for learners, including automated feedback (e.g. software applications with automated feedback, online tests with automated scoring, online polls with automated visual representations of results).

B2: I select digital technologies that can help in providing, receiving and analysing feedback in order to inform teaching and enhance the design of learning on a continuous basis (e.g. online polls and surveys, dashboards for managing grades and feedback, e-portfolios, context-dependent feedback).

C1: I reflect on and involve my students in using digital technologies for collection and analysis of feedback for planning further action (e.g. shared documents, blogs, mind mapping tools, reflective learning logs, learning journals, e-portfolios).

C2: I initiate and promote a strategy within my school and its wider community on the use of digital technologies that facilitate giving, receiving and analysing feedback, to support planning for further action (e.g. e-portfolios, context dependent feedback, digital storytelling).
I am not aware of this competence.

items.content: 4.1. Assessment - Assessment strategies Using digital technologies to support formative and summative assessment of learning.
4.2. Assessment - Analysing evidence Using digital technologies to collect and analyse evidence on students´ learning processes and outcomes.
4.3. Assessment - Feedback and planning Using digital technologies to provide feedback to learners, facilitating planning of further action.

interpretations.headline: Reflecting on competence 4.1
interpretations.summary: This response records the maturity statement you selected for this specific digital competence. The statements describe awareness, exploration, use, purposeful selection, reflective support and wider initiative in item-specific ways. A higher point value indicates a later self-described position in this framework; it does not establish better teaching or better student outcomes. The separate not-aware response is a valid starting point for learning. Use a recent example and your working conditions to put the choice in context. The displayed points preserve the original statement order: 0 = not aware; 1 = A1; 2 = A2; 3 = B1; 4 = B2; 5 = C1; 6 = C2. These codes are maturity statements within this framework, not agreement levels, teacher grades or population percentiles.

guidance.text: Choose one recent example connected with this competence. What did you do, what evidence did you notice, and which conditions helped or limited it?
Choose one question about students’ understanding. Collect a small amount of learning evidence and decide what you would change after seeing it.
Keep feedback and student data proportionate to the learning need, and use your school’s approved arrangements for data protection.

limitations: Fixed source: 2022 Toolkit Annex I for complete item text and A1–C2 labels; official2023 report p.11/Annex1 for seventh not-aware option and0–6 point mapping. The2023 report omits the B2 row for6.5; no omitted row was invented.
These are self-reported digital-competence positions, not observed teaching, student learning outcomes, professional certification, personality labels or a school/teacher ranking.

The six separate digital area units, instructions, feedback and conservative missing policy are project adaptations. Current online text, independent-area validity and Chinese-version validity were not established.

Missing answers remain null and are not treated as a zero-point not-aware response. Any missing competence makes this area invalid/incomplete for interpretation. Other area units have their own completeness; no missing value is imputed. This project policy is not claimed as an author-issued missing-data algorithm.

No area average, global192-point score, overall proficiency band, population norm, percentile or cross-tool total is supplied. Consult the official Toolkit and2023 report for original glossary and full-tool interpretation.
report.disclaimer: For supportive professional learning reflection by the teacher receiving their own authorized results. A1–C2 are this framework’s maturity codes, not grades for teacher quality. No EU endorsement, badge or certificate is issued. Existing access and feedback permissions still apply.

instruction.text: Reflect on your current professional digital practice. For each competence choose the ONE statement that best describes your current position. A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 are progressive, item-specific statements; they are not agreement ratings. If appropriate, choose “I am not aware of this competence”, which is a real zero-point answer. A missing response remains missing. This digital unit is one area of the fixed2022 SELFIEforTEACHERS Toolkit and uses the official per-item0–6 mapping described in2023. Feedback is for your professional learning, not teacher appraisal, EU certification or student-outcome prediction.
instruction.source: Project-written digital instruction grounded in JRC129699 Toolkit self-reflection navigation/AnnexI and JRC131282 p.11/Annex1; not a verbatim official platform instruction.
